attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

## Positioning vs Tool-Use Literature (Dream-driven addition)

**Critical gap identified by all 3 Dream tiers**: The core pipeline (counterfactual labels → SFT small classifier → selective invocation) is standard in tool-use learning. Must position against:
- **Toolformer** (Schick et al. 2024): Self-supervised tool-use learning via API call insertion. SimGate differs: hindsight labels from environment forking (not self-supervised), safety-aware framing (not general tool selection).
- **ART** (Paranjape et al. 2023): Automated tool selection via LLM reasoning. SimGate: dedicated lightweight router, not LLM-as-router.
- **Chameleon** (Lu et al. 2024): LLM-as-planner routing to diverse tools. SimGate: single modality (deterministic computation), explicit small router.
- **ToolkenGPT** (Hao et al. 2024): Token-level tool triggers. SimGate: step-level routing with counterfactual labels.

**Our differentiation**: (1) Episode-level counterfactual labeling — overcomes per-step oracle circularity in sparse-reward environments (98% tie rate), providing ground-truth episode outcomes rather than tie-break artifacts. (2) Empirical finding: death avoidance accounts for ~90% of routing signal [A] — quantifies WHERE and WHY tool invocation helps (catastrophic failure prevention, not positive guidance). (3) Diagnostic framework — counterfactual analysis + router as probe reveals systematic LLM failure modes across task categories. (4) The contribution is the finding + methodology, not the router architecture — this distinguishes from "we built a better tool selector" papers.

**Paper must include a dedicated Related Work section** (not just intro paragraphs). Minimum coverage: tool-use learning (Toolformer, ART, Chameleon), adaptive computation (CogRouter, ARES, Mixture-of-Depths), world model routing (ITP-R, Dyna-Think), agent frameworks (ReAct).

- **Problem**: LLM agents hallucinate state transitions on rule-governed environments (temperature physics, chemical reactions), leading to catastrophic failures. ITP-R routes to an approximate LLM world model but underperforms pure internal reasoning (62.58 vs CogRouter 84.6 on ScienceWorld). ReTool/AgentMath learn when to invoke code interpreters but use implicit routing entangled with the backbone. Tool-use learning methods (Toolformer, ART, Chameleon) learn general tool selection but don't specialize for catastrophic failure prevention or use counterfactual trajectory labeling.

- **Our framing**: We use episode-level counterfactual analysis to understand WHAT routing learns. Per-step oracle labeling degenerates (98% tie rate on ScienceWorld), so we run complete episodes under pure-internal and pure-deterministic strategies, comparing episode-level outcomes. Key finding: ~90% of routing signal is death avoidance [A] — deterministic computation's value is almost entirely concentrated in preventing catastrophic failures (-100 penalties). Non-death performance difference is small but non-negligible (Δ_nd=+2.84, 9.6% of Δ_full [A]).
